existing.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program funds 1-2 semesters of full-time master's-level study or full-time post-master's (doctoral/postdoctoral) study or research at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. Visegrad country nationals apply to study in another Visegrad country; EaP/WB country nationals apply to study in a Visegrad country. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester to the host institution. Applications for the 2027/28 cycle open on 1 January 2027 and close on 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM.
eligibility: Holds a bachelor's or master's degree
Citizenship or residence in Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia or an EaP/WB country
Country of citizenship differs from the country of the host institution
Previous levels of university studies completed in a country other than the country of application
Distance between current employer/university or permanent residence and the host university exceeds 150 km
Full-time study/research at master's or post-master's (doctoral, postdoc) level
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a bachelor's or master's degree and be citizens or residents of a Visegrad country (Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia) or an EaP/WB country; the host institution must be in a different country from the applicant's citizenship and more than 150 km from the applicant's current employer/university or permanent residence. Previous university study must have been completed in a country other than the one of application.
benefits: EUR 3,500 per semester stipend for the scholar
EUR 2,000 per semester paid to the host institution to cover the scholar's costs there
coverage: EUR 3,500 per semester paid to the scholar
EUR 2,000 per semester paid to the host institution
requirements: Submit through the My Visegrad online system at my.visegradfund.org
Upload all documents in one submission before the strict deadline
documents: Master's level: scanned valid ID document
Master's level: scanned transcript of records covering at least the last two completed semesters, or a diploma supplement
Master's level: scanned letter of acceptance from the host university (or proof of applying if not yet accepted)
Post-Master's level: scanned valid ID document
Post-Master's level: scanned letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan
Documents in English or accompanied by a certified translation
application_method: Online application via the My Visegrad system (http://my.visegradfund.org/)
Application must be submitted online by April 15, 12 PM (noon)
existing.selection_notes: Preference is given to applicants not previously supported and to applicants with study/research topics relevant to the V4 region. Results are normally published at the end of May; the funded stay can therefore only start from September/October at the earliest.
existing.best_fit: Master's and doctoral students and researchers from the Visegrad Four and the EaP/WB region seeking a 1-2 semester funded stay at an accredited institution in another participating country.
existing.notes: Sibling Visegrad instruments exist and are separate calls: Visegrad Fellowship (open till 30 November 2026), Visegrad Postdoc, and Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships (open till 30 September 2026).
existing.duration: 1-2 semesters of full-time master's-level study or full-time post-master's (doctoral/postdoctoral) study or research
existing.application_period: Annual cycle; call opens 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM and closes 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM for the 2027/28 academic year
existing.deadline_display: Official timeline for the 2027/28 cycle: 'Jan 1, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Call opens', 'Apr 15, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Final application deadline', 'May 31, 2027 at 12:00 PM: Results announced'. Applications must be submitted online via My Visegrad by April 15, 12 PM (noon).

scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
scholarships.official_source: World Bank, Development Economics Vice Presidency (programme funded by the Government of Japan)

existing.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.
eligibility: Be a national of a World Bank member developing country on the published 2027 eligible list
Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country
Hold a bachelor's (or equivalent) degree earned at least 3 years prior to the Application Deadline date

Be employed in development-related work in a paid full-time position at the time of submitting the scholarship application, with at least 3 years of paid development-related employment since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past 6 years from the date of the application deadline

On or before the scholarship application deadline date, be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) for the upcoming academic year to at least one of the JJ/WBGSP participating master's programs located outside of the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence listed at the time the call for scholarship applications opens; the letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

Not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment of the World Bank Group, and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Individuals who have previously been offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but declined it, or who previously received a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but did not graduate, are not eligible to apply again
Exception: applicants from a country on the list of Fragile and Conflict States in Annex 3 of the Application Guidelines may have their limited employment opportunities taken into consideration
existing.eligibility_summary: National of a listed World Bank developing country with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the application deadline, at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, and unconditional admission (except funding) to a JJ/WBGSP participating master's programme outside their country of citizenship and residence.
benefits: The scholarship covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Participation in the JJ/WBGSP alumni community of more than 7,000 mid-career professionals from 160 developing countries and Japan
coverage: Cost of basic medical insurance obtained through the university

Monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus during the scholarship period (accommodations, food, books); amount varies by host country and is not published on the programme page
Economy class air travel between the home country and the host university at the start of the study program and immediately after the scholarship period
US$600 travel allowance for each trip
requirements: Must already hold an unconditional admission letter (except for funding) from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence as listed when the call opened
The letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates who are admitted unconditionally (except for finance) to a participating master's program and shortlisted as eligible JJ/WBGSP applicants by the participating university
All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions; they will not change during an open call for applications
documents: Letter of admission from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program (must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application)
JJ/WBGSP application form, accessed through a link communicated only to candidates shortlisted by the participating university
application_method: Choose a target from the published list of participating master's programs for the relevant application window
Apply directly to that university and satisfy its own admission requirements and internal deadlines
Be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to the participating master's program
Ask the university whether you meet both conditions: unconditional admission and shortlisting as an eligible JJ/WBGSP applicant
Once the university shortlists you, it communicates the link to the JJ/WBGSP application form
Upload the admission letter and submit the JJ/WBGSP application within the application window
existing.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
existing.best_fit: Nationals of listed developing countries who hold a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline, have at least three years of paid development-related work experience acquired within the past six years, and can first secure unconditional admission (except funding) to one of only 44 participating master's programmes outside their country of citizenship and residence.
existing.notes: Not eligible if admitted to a non-participating programme: the World Bank states explicitly that if you are not admitted to one of the participating master's programs you are not eligible to apply for a JJ/WBGSP scholarship in 2027. The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you hold another award you must send those documents to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree. Declining an earlier offer, or receiving the scholarship and failing to graduate, permanently bars reapplication. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 developing-country-national cycle is live.
existing.duration: The duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
existing.application_period: Two application rounds per cycle, organised to match the academic calendars of the participating programmes. For the 2027 cycle: Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027; Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027. Each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
existing.deadline_display: Application Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027. The programme also runs Application Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating master's programme and shortlisted as eligible by that university.
